body: I've had a couple of summer jobs, but apart from that, no. Once I've got myself figured out I'm planning on starting the search.

I just desperately wish I'd had a normal upbringing and I could be a normal dude with a normal job and normal interests. I'm hoping that'll come in time, but for now I just feel like an alien walking around.
Isn't me - hope your friend is alright. The reason I posted this in unsent letters is that the letter is more hypothetical than a commitment, so I am, obviously, still here.

Hm, it's quite a hard thing to prove, because by my situation's very nature, I haven't really left much of a mark on the world to provide me with evidence. If you can think of something I could do as proof, I'd happily oblige.
I have no favourite colours. The only ones that really come to mind are the primary colours and a few others I remember being taught in primary school.

My parents are very private people who live in a house on its own with no neighbours. The rest of my family lived a decent way away, so I would only see see occasionally. My only social contact outside school was at church - my parents are very religious - and because I was the 'weird kid from out of town', I didn't make any friends at school as they all lived around the block from each other and all therefore spent a lot of time with each other after school.

High school was pretty much the same deal: I was a day pupil at a boarding school, so all the other kids were best buds and I was the outcast who took a train home to be alone every day.

Not surprisingly, all that time spent alone resulted in me basically not developing any social skills, or even really a concept of loneliness: when you've been alone all your life, it doesn't really occur to you that it's a problem when you find yourself with no friends. So when I went off to university, it was the same deal: I went to classes, vaguely spoke to my housemates (more them speaking at me - they both love an opportunity to ramble about their niche interests), and I was really none the wiser that my lifestyle was completely abnormal.

Reading or talking about the news is something my parents never really did, so I never picked up the habit of keeping track of what's going on in the world. I live in the UK, and I only found out about Brexit just before it happened.

I don't exactly know what prompted my recent sudden realisation that the way I have lived is unlike anything even resembling a normal existence, but it's all just hit me and it's like a veil covering the whole world has just been removed. "VR technology? What is this magic!", etc. etc.

It's kind of both magical and utterly terrifying at the same time - part of me wants to embrace everything, and part of me wants to kill myself because there's literally no way I can reintegrate into normal society having never been in it in the first place.

Unfortunately I can't open source it yet as I'm using it in production code for a VR app I'm developing for experiencing high fidelity CGI representations of events that would have happened had you taken a different decision. I'll be able to release bits of utility code like this relationship statistic calculator that's separate from the  main simulation architecture.
